title: [finding] two pending changesets still assert the per-package dedup sentence the CLI source forbids restating, and ship it to CHANGELOG
body:
Path: none | unreleased changeset claim | 硬时限:下次发版即固化

Filed by the `domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024, session `session_01QCdUBjM47SxioST9z5Zwdf`) out of the #18893 round (PR #19241), from that dev's `out_of_scope_findings` marked **「to file」**, class **(b)** — contradicts a declared contract. ⛔ Filed bare: `finding` only; `domain:*`, type and priority are triage's.

Dedupe words: `exactly the set the union could not see` · `18677 changeset` · `18778 changeset` · `CHANGELOG assertion` · `per-package dedup bound`.

## The shape

Two **pending, unreleased** changesets still state, as a **claim**, the sentence the CLI source explicitly forbids restating — and both **attribute it to source text that no longer says it**:

| file | the words it uses | why it is an assertion |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `.changeset/18677-validate-per-package-authoring-pass.md` | *"**By `compile.ts`' own description** the survivors of that second pass are «exactly the set the union could not see»"* | attributes the sentence to `compile.ts`, which now **prohibits** it |
| `.changeset/18778-lint-per-package-authoring-pass.md` | *"every finding that pass produces — «exactly the set the union could not see», **in the build command's own words**"* | attributes it to the build command, which no longer says it |

**The contract they contradict**, quoted from the tree:

- `packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts` — the entitled claim *"is narrower than"* that sentence, and the key is *"position-insensitive, ⛔ not collision-proof"*.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts` — *"⛔ Do not re-inflate that to"* it.

## ⚠️ Why this is worth a card rather than an acceptance note

**A changeset body ships verbatim into `CHANGELOG.md`.** These two are unreleased, so the cost of fixing is a diff; after the release that consumes them it is a published version number stating a falsehood to every upgrading reader — and an upgrading agent greps exactly that text. ⭐ This is the same clock that makes #18823 urgent, on one of the same files.

⛔ The 「somebody will touch this file anyway」 fallback does **not** hold for `.changeset/*` by the seat's own rule — which is precisely why this is filed rather than noted.

## ⭐ The third hit, checked and CLEARED — ⛔ not a miss

This seat re-derived the sweep over the **whole population** (482 changesets on `origin/main` `847e5773a`, whitespace-normalised because the sentence wraps across lines; lit control 481/482) and found **three** files, not two. The third is **legitimate** and is named here so nobody re-opens it:

- `.changeset/18779-per-package-dedup-positional-key.md` — *"**Also corrected:** the sentence «…», **which was false** for as long as the key was positional"*. That is a **quoted correction**, the settled shape, ⛔ not an assertion.

⚠️ This seat's first sweep printed **zero** rows while two direct reads each returned 1 — a contradiction that exposed a **broken instrument** (the loop double-prefixed `.changeset/`, reading paths that do not exist), ⛔ not a clean tree. Recorded because the zero was entirely convincing on its own.

## Successors, named

- **`.changeset/18677-…`** is the claimed file surface of in-flight card **#18823** (PR #18867), for a **different** defect (its declined `**BREAKING**` banner). ⇒ whoever lands that card is already opening this file and can carry this half. ⚠️ That card is `pm:awaiting-maintainer` and ⛔ must not be pre-empted.
- **`.changeset/18778-…`** has **no** named successor. It is the half that would otherwise be lost.

## First act for whoever takes this

Re-derive both quotes at `origin/main` **whitespace-normalised** — ⚠️ the sentence wraps across two lines and a line-oriented `grep -F` returns `0` on it. Triage, two seats and this card's own sweep have each paid for that zero once. Then write the replacement from the source's **settled** wording; ⛔ do not invent a fourth phrasing of a bound that already has three.
